title: Trello Review 2026: Is Atlassian's Visual Project Management Tool Still the King of Kanban?
content:
# Trello Review 2026: Is Atlassian's Visual Project Management Tool Still the King of Kanban?

*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

**Last updated: July 22, 2026**

---

## Quick Answer

**Trello 8.8/10** — Trello remains the most intuitive and visually approachable project management tool in 2026. Backed by Atlassian with 50M+ users worldwide, it excels at visual Kanban-style task management with a gentle learning curve that takes minutes — not days. The **Free plan** is genuinely useful for individuals and small teams (up to 10 collaborators per Workspace), and paid plans start at just **$5/user/month**. With AI features now integrated into Premium and Enterprise plans, Butler no-code automation, and 200+ Power-Up integrations, Trello is the best choice if you want a visual, lightweight, and easy-to-adopt project management tool. The trade-off: it lacks the depth of native features found in ClickUp, Monday.com, or Asana for complex project management needs like Gantt charts, time tracking, or resource management.

👉 [**Try Trello Free Today**](https://trello.com/)

---

## Rating Overview

| Category | Score |
|----------|-------|
| Ease of Use | 9.5/10 |
| Visual Interface | 9.5/10 |
| Features | 8.0/10 |
| Collaboration | 9.0/10 |
| Integrations | 9.0/10 |
| Automation | 8.5/10 |
| Value | 9.0/10 |
| Mobile | 8.5/10 |
| **Overall** | **8.8/10** |

---

## What We Like

- **Instant onboarding** — Trello's drag-and-drop Kanban interface is so intuitive that new users can start managing tasks within 5 minutes. No training sessions, no tutorials needed. 75% of organizations report value from Trello within the first 30 days (TechValidate survey).
- **Exceptional free tier** — Unlimited cards, up to 10 boards per Workspace, unlimited Power-Ups, mobile apps, 2FA, and 10 collaborators per Workspace. More generous than ClickUp's storage-limited free tier and Asana's 15-user cap. Ideal for solo users, freelancers, and micro-teams.
- **Butler automation (no-code)** — Trello's built-in automation engine lets you create rules, buttons, and scheduled commands without writing a single line of code. Automate repetitive workflows like moving cards, assigning members, setting due dates, and sending notifications. Standard plan includes 1,000 command runs/month; Premium and Enterprise get unlimited runs.
- **200+ Power-Up integrations** — Connect Trello with Slack, Google Drive, Dropbox, Jira, Confluence, Salesforce, GitHub, Microsoft Teams, Evernote, and dozens more. The Power-Up ecosystem turns Trello from a simple Kanban board into a connected command center.
- **AI-powered productivity** — Trello's AI (available on Premium and Enterprise) automatically summarizes cards, generates descriptions from quick notes, and turns forwarded emails into structured to-dos with AI-powered quick capture. The Inbox feature intelligently organizes incoming tasks.

---

## What We Don't Like

- **Limited native views on Free/Standard** — The Free and Standard plans are restricted to the classic Board view. Calendar, Timeline, Table, Dashboard, and Map views require the Premium plan at $10/user/month. Competitors like ClickUp include 15+ views even on their free plan.
- **No native time tracking** — Trello does not include built-in time tracking. You need a Power-Up like Clockify, Toggl, or Harvest to track billable hours. Competitors like ClickUp and Monday.com include native time tracking on all paid plans.
- **No Gantt charts on lower tiers** — The Timeline view (Trello's Gantt equivalent) is only available on Premium and Enterprise. Standard plan users are locked out of timeline-based planning, which is a standard feature on Asana and ClickUp's free plans.
- **File size limits on Free** — The Free plan limits attachments to 10MB per file. This is restrictive for teams sharing design files, videos, or large documents. Standard raises it to 250MB/file — still less than ClickUp's unlimited storage on paid plans.
- **Board limits on Free** — 10 boards per Workspace on the Free plan can feel restrictive for active users managing multiple projects. While you can archive old boards, this limit forces an upgrade for growing teams.

---

## Who Should Use Trello?

**Perfect for:**
- Small teams (2-25 people) who want a simple visual task manager
- Freelancers and solopreneurs managing client projects
- Marketing teams tracking content calendars and campaigns
- Remote teams who need a lightweight collaboration hub
- Agile teams running basic Kanban workflows
- Anyone who has tried complex PM tools and wants something simpler

**Not ideal for:**
- Enterprise teams needing advanced resource management, portfolio views, and complex reporting
- Teams requiring native time tracking and invoicing
- Large organizations needing granular permission controls on lower tiers
- Software development teams running Scrum with sprint planning, velocity tracking, and burndown charts (consider Jira instead)
- Users who need built-in document collaboration, whiteboards, and databases (consider Notion or ClickUp)

---

## Pricing Deep Dive

### Free Plan — $0/month
Unlimited cards, up to 10 boards per Workspace, up to 10 collaborators per Workspace, unlimited Power-Ups, Inbox, Planner (basic), unlimited activity log, assignee and due dates, iOS and Android apps, 2-factor authentication, custom backgrounds and stickers, 250 Workspace command runs/month, 10MB/file storage. **Best for: individuals and micro-teams testing the waters.**

### Standard Plan — $5/user/month (billed annually)
Everything in Free, plus: unlimited boards, AI-powered quick capture from email/Slack/Teams, Planner (full), advanced checklists, card mirroring, custom fields, list colors, collapsible lists, 250MB/file storage, 1,000 Workspace command runs/month, single board guests, saved searches. **Best for: small teams that need more boards and basic automation.**

### Premium Plan — $10/user/month (billed annually)
Everything in Standard, plus: AI features (card summarization, AI-generated descriptions), Calendar view, Timeline view, Table view, Dashboard view, Map view, Workspace-level views (Table and Calendar), unlimited Workspace command runs, admin and security features, Workspace-level templates, Collections, Observers, simple data export. **Best for: growing teams that need multiple views, AI features, and admin controls.**

### Enterprise Plan — $17.50/user/month (billed annually, ~$210/user/year)
Everything in Premium, plus: unlimited Workspaces, organization-wide permissions, organization-visible boards, public board management, multi-board guests, attachment permissions, Power-Up administration, free SSO and user provisioning with Atlassian Guard, 24/7 Enterprise Admin support. **Best for: large organizations with complex security requirements.**

---

## Feature-by-Feature Breakdown

### 1. Kanban Boards: The Core Experience

Trello's DNA is the Kanban board — a visual grid of lists (columns) containing cards (tasks). Each card can hold descriptions, checklists, due dates, attachments, labels, comments, custom fields, and links to other cards. The drag-and-drop interface is fluid, responsive, and genuinely enjoyable to use. You can watch a card move from "To Do" to "In Progress" to "Done" with a satisfying drag — a small UX detail that keeps teams engaged.

Cards support rich content: Markdown descriptions, unlimited checklists with due dates and assignees per item, file attachments from your computer or linked cloud services (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box), cover images, and custom fields (text, number, date, dropdown, checkbox).

Card mirroring — available on Standard and above — lets you display the same card on multiple boards. When you update the card on one board, it syncs everywhere. This is invaluable for cross-functional teams where a marketing task needs visibility on both the marketing board and the leadership dashboard.

### 2. Views: Beyond the Board

Trello has expanded beyond its Kanban roots with six distinct views:

- **Board View**: The classic Kanban interface. Available on all plans.
- **Timeline View**: Trello's Gantt-chart equivalent. Visualize tasks on a horizontal timeline, see dependencies, and identify bottlenecks. Premium and Enterprise only.
- **Calendar View**: See cards with due dates on a monthly or weekly calendar. Drag cards to reschedule. Premium and Enterprise only.
- **Table View**: A spreadsheet-style view of your cards. Sort, filter, and bulk-edit cards without opening each one. Premium and Enterprise only.
- **Dashboard View**: Create visual dashboards with charts, graphs, and metrics pulled from your board data. Track progress, workload, and KPIs at a glance. Premium and Enterprise only.
- **Map View**: Plot cards with location data on an interactive map. Useful for event planning, real estate, field operations. Premium and Enterprise only.

Workspace-level views (Table and Calendar) aggregate data across multiple boards, giving managers a bird's-eye view of all projects. This is a Premium feature and a significant upgrade for teams managing 5+ boards.

### 3. AI Features (2026)

Trello's AI integration — available on Premium and Enterprise — brings three main capabilities:

- **AI Quick Capture**: Forward an email to your Trello Inbox and AI transforms it into a structured card with extracted links, due dates, and action items. Similarly, messages sent from Slack or Teams are analyzed and summarized.
- **Card Summarization**: AI generates concise summaries of cards with long descriptions or extensive comment threads, helping team members get context faster.
- **AI-Generated Descriptions**: Start typing a card title and AI can generate a detailed description based on your brief input.

These AI features are helpful productivity boosters but not game-changers. They're most valuable for teams that process high volumes of incoming tasks from email and messaging platforms.

### 4. Butler Automation

Butler is Trello's no-code automation engine — and it's one of the platform's strongest features. You can create three types of automations:

- **Rules**: Trigger actions when specific events occur. Example: "When a card is moved to 'Done', mark the due date as complete and add a green label."
- **Buttons**: Create custom buttons on cards or boards that perform multiple actions at once. Example: A "Sprint Ready" button that assigns the card, sets a due date, adds it to the Sprint board, and notifies the assignee.
- **Scheduled Commands**: Run automations on a schedule. Example: "Every Monday at 9 AM, create a card in the Weekly Priorities list and notify the team."

Butler supports conditional logic, date-based triggers, and integration with external services via webhooks. The learning curve is minimal — the command builder uses natural language, so you type "when a card is moved into list 'Done' by anyone, add the green 'Complete' label" and Butler translates it into an automation.

**Command run limits:** Free = 250/month, Standard = 1,000/month, Premium/Enterprise = unlimited. For teams with heavy automation needs, the jump from Standard to Premium is justified by unlimited command runs alone.

### 5. Power-Ups and Integrations

Power-Ups are Trello's equivalent of apps or plugins. With 200+ Power-Ups available across all plans, you can extend Trello's functionality significantly:

- **Communication**: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Gmail, Outlook
- **File Storage**: Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box
- **Development**: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jira, Confluence
- **Design**: Figma, InVision, Miro, Lucidchart
- **CRM & Sales**: Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive
- **Time Tracking**: Clockify, Toggl, Harvest, TimeCamp
- **Reporting**: Planyway, Screenful, Blue Cat Reports
- **Forms**: Typeform, JotForm, Google Forms

The Power-Up directory is well-organized, and most Power-Ups are free. The key limitation: on Free and Standard, some Power-Ups require you to choose which ones to enable (though Free now supports unlimited Power-Ups per board). Enterprise plans can control which Power-Ups are available organization-wide.

### 6. Collaboration Features

Trello's collaboration model is straightforward and effective:

- **Comments**: @mention team members, attach files, use emoji reactions. Comments support Markdown for rich formatting.
- **Activity Log**: Every change is logged — card movements, description edits, checklist completions, comments. The activity log gives full transparency on who did what and when.
- **Notifications**: In-app, email, mobile push, and desktop notifications. You can customize notification preferences per board.
- **Guests**: Single-board guests on Standard; multi-board guests on Enterprise. Invite clients, freelancers, or stakeholders without giving them access to your entire Workspace.
- **Observer Role** (Premium): View-only access for stakeholders who need visibility without editing rights.

Trello's collaboration is intentionally lightweight — no built-in chat (beyond comments), no video conferencing, no document co-editing. For those, you integrate Slack, Zoom, and Google Docs via Power-Ups.

### 7. Mobile Experience

Trello's iOS and Android apps are well-designed and fully functional. The mobile Board view is optimized for smaller screens — swipe between lists horizontally, tap cards for detail views. You can create cards, set due dates, attach photos, add checklists, and leave comments from your phone.

The mobile apps support offline mode for viewing cached content, though changes require connectivity to sync. Push notifications keep you updated when you're away from your desk.

One notable mobile feature: Trello's home screen widget (iOS and Android) lets you see your most important cards at a glance without opening the app. Quick-add buttons let you capture ideas before you forget them.

---

## Trello vs. Competitors

### Trello vs. Asana
Asana offers deeper project management features — Gantt charts, portfolios, goals, workload management, and dependencies — across all paid plans. Trello's Timeline view (Gantt equivalent) is locked behind Premium at $10/user/month. Asana's free plan supports up to 15 users with unlimited tasks and projects, compared to Trello's 10 collaborators per Workspace. However, Trello is significantly more intuitive. Asana's interface can feel overwhelming for new users, while Trello's Kanban-first approach takes minutes to learn.

**Winner: Asana for complex project management; Trello for simplicity and visual task management.**

### Trello vs. Monday.com
Monday.com provides more native features — time tracking, Gantt charts, Kanban, forms, dashboards, and workload views — on its Basic plan ($12/seat/month). Trello restricts most views to Premium ($10/user/month). Monday.com's visual interface is colorful and intuitive, but its spreadsheet-like foundation can feel less "fun" than Trello's card-based system. Trello wins on price ($5 vs $12 for entry-level paid plans) and ease of adoption.

**Winner: Monday.com for feature-rich project management; Trello for budget-conscious visual collaboration.**

### Trello vs. ClickUp
ClickUp is the feature powerhouse — 15+ views (including Gantt, Mind Map, Workload, and Map), built-in Docs, Whiteboards, Goals, time tracking, and AI features all on the free plan. Trello cannot match ClickUp's feature density. However, ClickUp's learning curve is notoriously steep, and its interface can feel cluttered. Trello's focused simplicity is its competitive advantage. If you need one tool to do everything, choose ClickUp. If you want a tool your team will actually enjoy using daily, choose Trello.

**Winner: ClickUp for all-in-one power users; Trello for teams that value simplicity over feature count.**

### Trello vs. Notion
Notion is a workspace that combines docs, databases, wikis, and project management. Its flexibility is unmatched — you can build a Trello-style Kanban board inside Notion, alongside meeting notes, product specs, and company wikis. However, Notion requires significant setup and customization. Trello works out of the box. Notion is better for teams that want a single source of truth for all company knowledge. Trello is better for teams that just want to manage tasks visually.

**Winner: Notion for knowledge management and flexibility; Trello for focused task management.**

---

## Real-World Performance and Adoption

Trello's longevity and user base speak volumes:

- **50 million+ users** worldwide as of 2026, spanning individuals, startups, and Fortune 500 companies
- **75% of organizations** report measurable value from Trello within 30 days of deployment (TechValidate survey)
- **Used by**: Visa, Coinbase, John Deere, Zoom, Grand Hyatt, Fender, and thousands of other recognizable brands
- **Acquired by Atlassian** in 2017 for $425 million, ensuring long-term stability and deep integration with the Atlassian ecosystem (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket)
- **G2 Rating**: 4.4/5 stars across 23,000+ reviews — consistently praised for ease of use, visual interface, and quick setup
- **Available in 21 languages**, including Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, and Chinese

Trello's parent company, Atlassian, reported over $4.4 billion in annual revenue for FY2025, with Trello contributing significantly to its work management portfolio. The platform receives regular feature updates and security patches, with SOC 2 Type II certification, GDPR compliance, and enterprise-grade encryption (TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest).

---

## Setup and Onboarding

Getting started with Trello takes less than 5 minutes:

1. **Sign up** at trello.com with email, Google, Microsoft, Apple, or Slack account
2. **Create a Workspace** — name it after your team or project
3. **Create a Board** — start from scratch or choose from 100+ templates (Project Management, Sales CRM, Content Calendar, Sprint Retrospective, Remote Team Hub, and more)
4. **Add Lists** — common defaults are "To Do", "Doing", and "Done"
5. **Add Cards** — click "+ Add a card", give it a title, press Enter. Open the card to add descriptions, checklists, due dates, and members.

The learning curve is nearly flat. Trello's interface uses familiar concepts — boards, lists, cards — that map directly to real-world task management. Team members without any project management experience can become productive in their first session.

Trello also offers:
- **Interactive product tours** for new Workspace members
- **A comprehensive guide** (9 chapters covering basics to advanced automation)
- **Template gallery** with 100+ pre-built board templates by use case
- **Trello Community** with forums, tips, and user-submitted automations

---

## Security and Compliance

Trello benefits from Atlassian's enterprise-grade security infrastructure:

- **SOC 2 Type II certified** — independently audited security controls
- **GDPR compliant** — data processing agreements, data residency options, right to erasure
- **ISO 27001 certified** — information security management
- **Encryption**: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest
- **Two-factor authentication** (2FA) available on all plans — via authenticator app, SMS, or security key
- **SSO (Single Sign-On)**: Available on Enterprise plan via Atlassian Guard (SAML, Azure AD, Okta, OneLogin)
- **Data residency**: Enterprise customers can choose where their data is stored
- **Audit logs**: Premium and Enterprise plans include detailed activity and admin audit logs
- **Custom permissions**: Board-level and Workspace-level permissions; Enterprise adds organization-wide controls, attachment restrictions, and Power-Up governance

For regulated industries (finance, healthcare, government), the Enterprise plan with Atlassian Guard provides the necessary controls.

---

## Pros and Cons Summary

### Pros
✅ Incredible ease of use — 5-minute learning curve
✅ Beautiful, intuitive Kanban interface
✅ Generous Free plan (unlimited cards, up to 10 boards)
✅ Butler no-code automation across all plans
✅ 200+ Power-Up integrations
✅ AI features on Premium and Enterprise
✅ Strong mobile apps (iOS/Android)
✅ Atlassian-backed stability and security
✅ 50M+ users with an active template community
✅ SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001 compliance

### Cons
❌ Limited views on Free and Standard (only Board view)
❌ No native time tracking (requires Power-Up)
❌ No Gantt/Timeline on lower tiers
❌ 10MB/file attachment limit on Free plan
❌ 10-board limit on Free plan
❌ No built-in document editor (unlike Notion/ClickUp)
❌ Limited advanced PM features (resource management, portfolios, baselines)
❌ Can become chaotic with 50+ cards per board without disciplined organization

---

## Final Verdict

Trello 8.8/10 — Trello is the best visual project management tool for teams that prioritize simplicity, speed of adoption, and user enjoyment. Its Kanban boards are the industry standard for a reason: they're beautiful, responsive, and require zero training. The Free plan is genuinely capable for individuals and small teams, and the paid plans are competitively priced at $5-$17.50/user/month.

Where Trello excels — visual task management, team collaboration, quick onboarding, no-code automation — it is unmatched. Where it falls short — native time tracking, Gantt charts on lower tiers, advanced reporting, resource management — power users should look at ClickUp, Monday.com, or Asana.

The 2026 AI features are a welcome addition, particularly AI-powered quick capture from email and messaging apps. Butler automation continues to be a standout feature that saves teams hours of manual work.

For most small to medium teams looking for a project management tool that people will actually use (not just the project manager), Trello is the right choice. It won't replace every tool in your stack, but it will become the one your team opens first every morning.

👉 [**Start with Trello Free Today**](https://trello.com/)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Trello really free?
Yes. The Free plan includes unlimited cards, up to 10 boards per Workspace, unlimited Power-Ups per board, mobile apps, 2FA, and support for up to 10 collaborators per Workspace. There are no time limits or credit card requirements. It is genuinely free forever — not a trial.

### What's the difference between Trello Free and Standard?
Standard ($5/user/month) adds unlimited boards (vs. 10 on Free), AI-powered quick capture, advanced checklists, card mirroring, custom fields, 250MB/file attachments (vs. 10MB), 1,000 automation command runs/month (vs. 250), single-board guests, and saved searches. For teams hitting the 10-board limit or needing custom fields, Standard is the logical step up.

### Does Trello have Gantt charts?
Yes — the Timeline view, available on Premium ($10/user/month) and Enterprise ($17.50/user/month), provides Gantt chart-like functionality. You can visualize cards on a horizontal timeline, set dependencies, and identify scheduling conflicts. It is not available on Free or Standard plans.

### Can I use Trello for Agile/Scrum?
Trello supports basic Kanban out of the box, which is suitable for lightweight Agile workflows. For full Scrum (sprint planning, velocity tracking, burndown charts, story points), Trello requires Power-Ups like Planyway, Screenful, or Corrello. For dedicated Agile/Scrum teams, consider Atlassian's Jira instead — it integrates deeply with Trello via Power-Ups.

### How does Trello's AI work?
Trello's AI (Premium and Enterprise) provides three capabilities: (1) AI Quick Capture transforms forwarded emails and Slack/Teams messages into structured cards with summaries and links, (2) Card Summarization generates concise overviews of cards with long descriptions or extensive comment threads, and (3) AI-Generated Descriptions creates detailed card descriptions from brief titles or bullet points.

### Does Trello work offline?
Partial offline support is available on mobile apps. You can view recently accessed boards and cards offline, but you cannot create or edit cards until connectivity is restored. The desktop web app requires an internet connection.

### Can I import data from Asana, Monday.com, or ClickUp?
Yes. Trello supports direct imports from Asana, Monday.com, Todoist, and Wrike. You can also import data via CSV files for other tools. Boards, lists, cards, checklists, and due dates are preserved during import. Trello also offers a board-to-board copy feature for duplicating templates across Workspaces.

### How secure is Trello?
Trello benefits from Atlassian's enterprise security infrastructure: SOC 2 Type II certification, GDPR compliance, ISO 27001 certification, TLS 1.3 encryption in transit, AES-256 encryption at rest, and 2FA on all plans. Enterprise customers get SSO via Atlassian Guard, data residency options, audit logs, and organization-wide permission controls.

### What are Trello Power-Ups?
Power-Ups are integrations and feature extensions that add functionality to your Trello boards. With 200+ available, they span categories like file storage (Google Drive, Dropbox), communication (Slack, Teams), development (GitHub, Jira), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), time tracking (Toggl, Clockify), and reporting (Planyway, Screenful). Most Power-Ups are free and can be enabled per board.

### Does Trello have a desktop app?
Yes. Trello offers desktop apps for Windows and macOS, downloadable from trello.com/platforms. The desktop apps support native notifications, keyboard shortcuts, and system tray integration. The web app (trello.com) offers identical functionality.

### Can I use Trello for personal task management?
Absolutely. Trello is one of the best personal task management tools available. Create boards for different areas of your life (Work, Personal, Side Projects, Home), use checklists for recurring routines (daily habits, weekly reviews, packing lists), and leverage Butler automation for personal workflows (e.g., "every Monday at 8 AM, add a card to my Weekly Goals list"). The Free plan covers most personal use cases with ease.
